ESV.1: The oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for Tyre is laid waste, without house or harbor! From the land of Cyprus  it is revealed to them.
ESV.2: Be still, O inhabitants of the coast; the merchants of Sidon, who cross the sea, have filled you.
ESV.3: And on many waters your revenue was the grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile; you were the merchant of the nations.
ESV.4: Be ashamed, O Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea, saying: “I have neither labored nor given birth, I have neither reared young men nor brought up young women.”
ESV.5: When the report comes to Egypt, they will be in anguish  over the report about Tyre.
ESV.6: Cross over to Tarshish; wail, O inhabitants of the coast!
ESV.7: Is this your exultant city whose origin is from days of old, whose feet carried her to settle far away?
ESV.8: Who has purposed this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, whose merchants were princes, whose traders were the honored of the earth?
ESV.9: The LORD of hosts has purposed it, to defile the pompous pride of all glory,  to dishonor all the honored of the earth.
ESV.10: Cross over your land like the Nile, O daughter of Tarshish; there is no restraint anymore.
ESV.11: He has stretched out his hand over the sea; he has shaken the kingdoms; the LORD has given command concerning Canaan to destroy its strongholds.
ESV.12: And he said: “You will no more exult, O oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon; arise, cross over to Cyprus, even there you will have no rest.”
ESV.13: Behold the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that was not;  Assyria destined it for wild beasts. They erected their siege towers, they stripped her palaces bare, they made her a ruin.
ESV.14: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is laid waste.
ESV.15: In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days  of one king. At the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
ESV.16: “Take a harp; go about the city, O forgotten prostitute! Make sweet melody; sing many songs, that you may be remembered.”
ESV.17: At the end of seventy years, the LORD will visit Tyre, and she will return to her wages and will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.
ESV.18: Her merchandise and her wages will be holy to the LORD. It will not be stored or hoarded, but her merchandise will supply abundant food and fine clothing for those who dwell before the LORD.

NKJV.1: The burden against Tyre. Wail, you ships of Tarshish! For it is laid waste, So that there is no house, no harbor; From the land of Cyprus it is revealed to them.
NKJV.2: Be still, you inhabitants of the coastland, You merchants of Sidon, Whom those who cross the sea have filled.
NKJV.3: And on great waters the grain of Shihor, The harvest of the River, is her revenue; And she is a marketplace for the nations.

NKJV.9: The LORD of hosts has purposed it, To bring to dishonor the pride of all glory, To bring into contempt all the honorable of the earth.

NASB.1: The oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, O ships of Tarshish, For [Tyre] is destroyed, without house [or] harbor; It is reported to them from the land of Cyprus.
NASB.2: Be silent, you inhabitants of the coastland, You merchants of Sidon; Your messengers crossed the sea
NASB.3: And [were] on many waters. The grain of the Nile, the harvest of the River was her revenue; And she was the market of nations.
NASB.4: Be ashamed, O Sidon; For the sea speaks, the stronghold of the sea, saying, 'I have neither travailed nor given birth, I have neither brought up young men [nor] reared virgins.'
NASB.5: When the report [reaches] Egypt, They will be in anguish at the report of Tyre.
NASB.6: Pass over to Tarshish; Wail, O inhabitants of the coastland.
NASB.7: Is this your jubilant [city], Whose origin is from antiquity, Whose feet used to carry her to colonize distant places?
NASB.8: Who has planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, Whose merchants were princes, whose traders were the honored of the earth?
NASB.9: The LORD of hosts has planned it, to defile the pride of all beauty, To despise all the honored of the earth.
NASB.10: Overflow your land like the Nile, O daughter of Tarshish, There is no more restraint.
NASB.11: He has stretched His hand out over the sea, He has made the kingdoms tremble; The LORD has given a command concerning Canaan to demolish its strongholds.
NASB.12: He has said, 'You shall exult no more, O crushed virgin daughter of Sidon. Arise, pass over to Cyprus; even there you will find no rest.'
NASB.13: Behold, the land of the Chaldeans-- this is the people [which] was not; Assyria appointed it for desert creatures-- they erected their siege towers, they stripped its palaces, they made it a ruin.
NASB.14: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, For your stronghold is destroyed.
NASB.15: Now in that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will happen to Tyre as [in] the song of the harlot:
NASB.16: Take [your] harp, walk about the city, O forgotten harlot; Pluck the strings skillfully, sing many songs, That you may be remembered.
NASB.17: It will come about at the end of seventy years that the LORD will visit Tyre. Then she will go back to her harlot's wages and will play the harlot with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
NASB.18: Her gain and her harlot's wages will be set apart to the LORD; it will not be stored up or hoarded, but her gain will become sufficient food and choice attire for those who dwell in the presence of the LORD.

NLT.1:
This message came to me concerning Tyre: Wail, you trading ships of Tarshish,
for the harbor and houses of Tyre are gone!
The rumors you heard in Cyprus
are all true.
NLT.2:
Mourn in silence, you people of the coast
and you merchants of Sidon.
Your traders crossed the sea,
NLT.3:
sailing over deep waters.
They brought you grain from Egypt
and harvests from along the Nile.
You were the marketplace of the world.
NLT.4:
But now you are put to shame, city of Sidon,
for Tyre, the fortress of the sea, says,
“Now I am childless;
I have no sons or daughters.”
NLT.5:
When Egypt hears the news about Tyre,
there will be great sorrow.
NLT.6:
Send word now to Tarshish!
Wail, you people who live in distant lands!
NLT.7:
Is this silent ruin all that is left of your once joyous city?
What a long history was yours!
Think of all the colonists you sent to distant places.
NLT.8:
Who has brought this disaster on Tyre,
that great creator of kingdoms?
Her traders were all princes,
her merchants were nobles.
NLT.9:
The LORD of Heaven’s Armies has done it
to destroy your pride
and bring low all earth’s nobility.
NLT.10:
Come, people of Tarshish,
sweep over the land like the flooding Nile,
for Tyre is defenseless.
NLT.11:
The LORD held out his hand over the sea
and shook the kingdoms of the earth.
He has spoken out against Phoenicia,
ordering that her fortresses be destroyed.
NLT.12:
He says, “Never again will you rejoice,
O daughter of Sidon, for you have been crushed.
Even if you flee to Cyprus,
you will find no rest.”
NLT.13:
Look at the land of Babylonia —
the people of that land are gone!
The Assyrians have handed Babylon over
to the wild animals of the desert.
They have built siege ramps against its walls,
torn down its palaces,
and turned it to a heap of rubble.
NLT.14:
Wail, you ships of Tarshish,
for your harbor is destroyed!
NLT.15: For seventy years, the length of a king’s life, Tyre will be forgotten. But then the city will come back to life as in the song about the prostitute:
NLT.16:
Take a harp and walk the streets,
you forgotten harlot.
Make sweet melody and sing your songs
so you will be remembered again.
NLT.17: Yes, after seventy years the LORD will revive Tyre. But she will be no different than she was before. She will again be a prostitute to all kingdoms around the world.
NLT.18: But in the end her profits will be given to the LORD. Her wealth will not be hoarded but will provide good food and fine clothing for the LORD’s priests.

AMP.1:
The [mournful, inspired] oracle ( a burden to be carried) concerning Tyre:
Wail, O ships of Tarshish,
For Tyre is destroyed, without house, without harbor;
It is reported to them from the land of Cyprus (Kittim).
AMP.2:
Be silent, you inhabitants of the coastland,
You merchants of Sidon;
Your messengers crossed the sea
AMP.3:
And they were on great waters.
The grain of the Shihor, the harvest of the Nile River, was Tyre's revenue;
And she was the market of nations.
AMP.4:
Be ashamed, O Sidon [mother-city of Tyre, now like a widow bereaved of her children];
For the sea speaks, the stronghold of the sea, saying,
"I have neither labored nor given birth [to children];
I have neither brought up young men nor reared virgins."
AMP.5:
When the report reaches Egypt,
They will be in agony at the report about Tyre.
AMP.6:
Cross over to Tarshish [to seek safety as exiles];
Wail, O inhabitants of the coastland [of Tyre].
AMP.7:
Is this your jubilant city,
Whose origin dates back to antiquity,
Whose feet used to carry her [far away] to colonize distant places?
AMP.8:
Who has planned this against Tyre, the bestower of crowns,
Whose merchants were princes, whose traders were the honored of the earth?
AMP.9:
The LORD of hosts has planned it, to defile the pride of all beauty,
To bring into contempt and humiliation all the honored of the earth.
AMP.10:
Overflow your land like [the overflow of] the Nile, O Daughter of Tarshish;
There is no more restraint [on you to make you pay tribute to Tyre].
AMP.11:
He has stretched out His hand over the sea,
He has shaken the kingdoms;
The LORD has given a command concerning Canaan to destroy her strongholds and her fortresses [like Tyre and Sidon].
AMP.12:
He has said, "You shall never again exult [in triumph], O crushed Virgin Daughter of Sidon.
Arise, cross over to Cyprus; even there you will find no rest."
AMP.13: Now look at the land of the Chaldeans (Babylonia)—this is the people which was not; the Assyrians allocated Tyre for desert creatures—they set up their siege towers, they stripped its palaces, they made it a ruin.
AMP.14:
Wail, O ships of Tarshish,
For your stronghold [of Tyre] is destroyed.
AMP.15: Now in that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king. At the end of seventy years it will happen to Tyre as in the prostitute's song:
AMP.16:
Take a harp, walk around the city,
O forgotten prostitute;
Play the strings skillfully, sing many songs,
That you may be remembered.
AMP.17: It will come to pass at the end of seventy years that the LORD will remember Tyre. Then she will return to her prostitute's wages and will play the [role of a] prostitute [by trading] with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
AMP.18: But her commercial gain and her prostitute's wages will be dedicated to the LORD; it will not be treasured or stored up, but her commercial gain will become sufficient food and stately clothing for those who dwell (minister) in the presence of the LORD.

NET.1: Here is a message about Tyre: Wail, you large ships, for the port is too devastated to enter! From the land of Cyprus this news is announced to them.
NET.2: Lament, you residents of the coast, you merchants of Sidon who travel over the sea, whose agents sail over
NET.3: the deep waters! Grain from the Shihor region, crops grown near the Nile she receives; she is the trade center of the nations.
NET.4: Be ashamed, O Sidon, for the sea says this, O fortress of the sea: “I have not gone into labor or given birth; I have not raised young men or brought up young women.”
NET.5: When the news reaches Egypt, they will be shaken by what has happened to Tyre.
NET.6: Travel to Tarshish! Wail, you residents of the coast!
NET.7: Is this really your boisterous city whose origins are in the distant past, and whose feet led her to a distant land to reside?
NET.8: Who planned this for royal Tyre, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the dignitaries of the earth?
NET.9: The LORD who commands armies planned it — to dishonor the pride that comes from all her beauty, to humiliate all the dignitaries of the earth.
NET.10: Daughter Tarshish, travel back to your land, as one crosses the Nile; there is no longer any marketplace in Tyre.
NET.11: The LORD stretched out his hand over the sea, he shook kingdoms; he gave the order to destroy Canaan’s fortresses.
NET.12: He said, “You will no longer celebrate, oppressed virgin daughter Sidon! Get up, travel to Cyprus, but you will find no relief there.”
NET.13: Look at the land of the Chaldeans, these people who have lost their identity! The Assyrians have made it a home for wild animals. They erected their siege towers, demolished its fortresses, and turned it into a heap of ruins.
NET.14: Wail, you large ships, for your fortress is destroyed!
NET.15: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the typical life span of a king. At the end of seventy years Tyre will try to attract attention again, like the prostitute in the popular song:
NET.16: “Take the harp, go through the city, forgotten prostitute! Play it well, play lots of songs, so you’ll be noticed!”
NET.17: At the end of seventy years the LORD will revive Tyre. She will start making money again by selling her services to all the earth’s kingdoms.
NET.18: Her profits and earnings will be set apart for the LORD. They will not be stored up or accumulated, for her profits will be given to those who live in the LORD’s presence and will be used to purchase large quantities of food and beautiful clothes.

MSG.1:
Wail, ships of Tarshish,
your strong seaports all in ruins!
When the ships returned from Cyprus,
they saw the destruction.
MSG.2:
Hold your tongue, you who live on the seacoast,
merchants of Sidon.
Your people sailed the deep seas,
buying and selling,
MSG.3:
Making money on wheat from Shihor,
grown along the Nile—
multinational broker in grains!
MSG.4:
Hang your head in shame, Sidon. The Sea speaks up,
the powerhouse of the ocean says,
"I've never had labor pains, never had a baby,
never reared children to adulthood,
Never gave life, never worked with life.
It was all numbers, dead numbers, profit and loss."
MSG.5:
When Egypt gets the report on Tyre,
what wailing! what wringing of hands!
MSG.6:
Visit Tarshish, you who live on the seacoast.
Take a good, long look and wail—yes, cry buckets of tears!
MSG.7:
Is this the city you remember as energetic and alive,
bustling with activity, this historic old city,
Expanding throughout the globe,
buying and selling all over the world?
MSG.8:
And who is behind the collapse of Tyre,
the Tyre that controlled the world markets?
Tyre's merchants were the business tycoons.
Tyre's traders called all the shots.
MSG.9:
God-of-the-Angel-Armies ordered the crash
to show the sordid backside of pride
and puncture the inflated reputations.
MSG.10:
Sail for home, O ships of Tarshish.
There are no docks left in this harbor.
MSG.11:
God reached out to the sea and sea traders,
threw the sea kingdoms into turmoil.
God ordered the destruction
of the seacoast cities, the centers of commerce.
MSG.12:
God said, "There's nothing left here to be proud of,
bankrupt and bereft Sidon.
Do you want to make a new start in Cyprus?
Don't count on it. Nothing there will work out for you either."
MSG.13: Look at what happened to Babylon: There's nothing left of it. Assyria turned it into a desert, into a refuge for wild dogs and stray cats. They brought in their big siege engines, tore down the buildings, and left nothing behind but rubble.
MSG.14:
Wail, ships of Tarshish,
your strong seaports all in ruins!
MSG.15: For the next seventy years, a king's lifetime, Tyre will be forgotten. At the end of the seventy years, Tyre will stage a comeback, but it will be the comeback of a worn-out whore, as in the song:
MSG.16:
"Take a harp, circle the city,
unremembered whore.
Sing your old songs, your many old songs.
Maybe someone will remember."
MSG.17: At the end of the seventy years, God will look in on Tyre. She'll go back to her old whoring trade, selling herself to the highest bidder, doing anything with anyone—promiscuous with all the kingdoms of earth—for a fee.
MSG.18: But everything she gets, all the money she takes in, will be turned over to God. It will not be put in banks. Her profits will be put to the use of God-Aware, God-Serving-People, providing plenty of food and the best of clothing.

NIV.1:
A Prophecy About Tyre
An oracle concerning Tyre:
Wail, O ships of Tarshish!
For Tyre is destroyed
and left without house or harbor.
From the land of Cyprus
word has come to them.
NIV.2:
Be silent, you people of the island
and you merchants of Sidon,
whom the seafarers have enriched.
NIV.3:
On the great waters
came the grain of the Shihor;
the harvest of the Nile was the revenue of Tyre,
and she became the marketplace of the nations.
NIV.4:
Be ashamed, O Sidon, and you, O fortress of the sea,
for the sea has spoken:
“I have neither been in labor nor given birth;
I have neither reared sons nor brought up daughters.”
NIV.5:
When word comes to Egypt,
they will be in anguish at the report from Tyre.
NIV.6:
Cross over to Tarshish;
wail, you people of the island.
NIV.7:
Is this your city of revelry,
the old, old city,
whose feet have taken her
to settle in far-off lands?
NIV.8:
Who planned this against Tyre,
the bestower of crowns,
whose merchants are princes,
whose traders are renowned in the earth?
NIV.9:
The Lord Almighty planned it,
to bring low the pride of all glory
and to humble all who are renowned on the earth.
NIV.10:
Till your land as along the Nile,
O Daughter of Tarshish,
for you no longer have a harbor.
NIV.11:
The Lord has stretched out his hand over the sea
and made its kingdoms tremble.
He has given an order concerning Phoenicia
that her fortresses be destroyed.
NIV.12:
He said, “No more of your reveling,
O Virgin Daughter of Sidon, now crushed!
“Up, cross over to Cyprus;
even there you will find no rest.”
NIV.13:
Look at the land of the Babylonians,
this people that is now of no account!
The Assyrians have made it
a place for desert creatures;
they raised up their siege towers,
they stripped its fortresses bare
and turned it into a ruin.
NIV.14:
Wail, you ships of Tarshish;
your fortress is destroyed!
NIV.15: At that time Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the span of a king’s life. But at the end of these seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song of the prostitute:
NIV.16:
“Take up a harp, walk through the city,
O prostitute forgotten;
play the harp well, sing many a song,
so that you will be remembered.”
NIV.17: At the end of seventy years, the Lord will deal with Tyre. She will return to her hire as a prostitute and will ply her trade with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.
NIV.18: Yet her profit and her earnings will be set apart for the Lord; they will not be stored up or hoarded. Her profits will go to those who live before the Lord, for abundant food and fine clothes.
